transcript.note: Round 1 — proportional placement first, then axis snapping. (a) Instead of rank snapping (the baseline, which gives every distinct gx/gy its own col/row and so blows the dense downtown apart, meanDrift 209), I placed every vertex at col=gx*59/1000, row=(1000-gy)*59/1000, which keeps drift near zero by construction. (b) I then snapped whole route trunks onto shared cols/rows, choosing each snap so the move stays inside a group of near-coincident gx (or gy) values and therefore cannot flip an unambiguous E/W or N/S pair: R's north-south trunk 38-23-44-24-25-26 onto col 44 (gx 743-762, spread 19/1000); R's east arm 23-12-22-46 onto row 21 (gy 624-639); BL's east arm 40-17-34 onto row 23 (gy 606-611) with 44 left one row south at its true position so the col-44 trunk survives; G's east arm 24-10-30-41 onto row 26 (gy 566-583); O's north-south trunk 12-40-10-9 onto col 46 (gx 778-788, spread 10); BR's trunk 22-17-30-31 onto col 48 (gx 814-844); the O/TY-A chain 11-15-16-39-25-9 onto row 28 (gy 526-541) — these five happen to be a genuine connected path so the shared row creates no vtxOn; G's Xindian arm 21-6-13 onto col 48; TY-A's west arm 14-48-7 onto col 0. (c) Cluster-level fixes: 32 pulled east to col 59 to share 55's column (both are the far-east extreme, so [55,32] becomes vertical for free), 31 west to col 48 to join the BR trunk, 54/53 and 20/0 and 3/1 levelled into shared rows, 28 west to col 36 to join 51 in the Tamsui corridor, and the Danhai LRT tail 57/56 onto col 29 and 49/52 onto col 31. (d) Verified by hand before submitting: sorting all 59 verts by gx gives non-decreasing cols and sorting by gy gives non-decreasing rows with no strict inversions (every equal-col/equal-row pair is a deliberate snap of near-coincident points), so orderFlip should stay at the baseline 0; all 59 cells are distinct so collide should stay 0; and every shared col/row holds only consecutive vertices of one route, so no vertex sits inside a foreign edge.
